history.period: CONFLICT - one crowdsourced listing claims 1890 CE, but its own narrative says precise builder and date are elusive; treat as 20th century, UNVERIFIED
history.summary: A small community Hindu temple dedicated to Vishwakarma, the divine architect and patron of craftsmen, at Mission Veng, Lawngtlai (PIN 796891). One crowdsourced heritage listing describes it as a simple single-storey yellow-painted hall with a plain sanctum and large windows overlooking the hills. Its stated 'Year Built 1890 CE' is almost certainly spurious - Lawngtlai was a minor settlement in 1890 and Mizoram had virtually no Hindu presence then; the listing's own text admits builder and date details are elusive, and its claims of an ASI/state-archaeology survey and of 'Bengal Renaissance Period'/'Kalinga-Nagara-Dravidian' pedigree should not be repeated as fact. Coordinates (22.53199, 92.89306) come from that listing and are approximate (verify). No reliable image of the actual temple was found after genuine searching.

name: Vishwakarma Mandir
town_description: Lawngtlai is the district headquarters of Lawngtlai district in southern Mizoram, close to the Myanmar border. It is home to the Lai tribe and, like the rest of Mizoram, is overwhelmingly Christian; a small Hindu minority of traders, government staff and paramilitary personnel maintains the town's few community temples.
